body:
Multiplying with Area Models: 1. 35 is 5 times as many as 7 (also: 35 is 7 times as many as 5). 2. 240 + 18 = 258. 3. 1,200 + 80 + 24 = 1,304. 4. 7,000 + 1,400 + 0 + 35 = 8,435. 5. 200 + 100 + 30 + 15 = 345. 6. 600 + 120 + 80 + 24 = 884. 7. Each partial product (20 × 10, 20 × 5, 3 × 10, 3 × 5) is the area of one of the four rectangles; their sum is the whole area.
Times as Many: 1. 6 × 4 = b; b = 24 inches. 2. 7 × d = 56 (or 56 ÷ 7 = d); d = 8 stickers. 3. 435 tickets. 4. 6 times as tall (18 ÷ 3 = 6). 5. 360 muffins. 6. 1,026 corn plants. 7. Ana has 36 and Leo has 15; Ana has 21 more.
Sharing and Remainders: 1. 80 ÷ 4 = 20 and 16 ÷ 4 = 4, so 24. 2. 26 R 2. 3. 412; 412 × 3 = 1,236. 4. 75 ÷ 8 = 9 R 3; 10 vans, because the 3 extra students still need a ride. 5. 8 full pieces; 2 inches left over. 6. 7 cards each; 2 left over. 7. 6 × 124 = 744; 744 − 94 = 650; 650 ÷ 9 = 72 R 2, so 73 boxes. Estimate: 6 × 125 = 750, minus about 100 is about 650, and 650 ÷ 9 is a little more than 70, so 73 boxes is reasonable.
Multiplication and Division Check: 1. 3,090. 2. 1,504 (1,200 + 80 + 210 + 14). 3. 8,180. 4. 142. 5. 142 R 6. 6. 48 is 6 times as many as 8 (or 8 times as many as 6). 7. 9 × 4 = t; t = 36 feet. 8. 214 ÷ 6 = 35 R 4, so 36 boxes; the last 4 cupcakes need a box too. 9. 18 × 24 = 432 seats; 432 − 389 = 43 empty seats. Estimate: 20 × 24 = 480 is a little high, and about 430 − 390 = 40 is close to 43.
Scoring tip: for remainder problems, a correct quotient with the remainder handled wrongly for the story (9 vans) is Developing on accuracy; the reasoning criterion rewards an explanation of the remainder.
title: Answer key: Multiplying and Dividing Bigger Numbers
